questions.q: Why is SQL Server on an Azure VM described as genuinely full IaaS?
options: Because it is the actual SQL Server binary running on a VM you provision, behaving exactly like an on-prem instance — you manage the OS and SQL Server patching yourself
Because Microsoft manages the OS and SQL Server patching automatically, like the other two options
Because it has less SQL Server feature coverage than Azure SQL Database
Because it requires a dedicated VNet subnet like Managed Instance
questions.explain: This closes the loop from Lesson 4's IaaS/PaaS mapping — full control, full obligation.

questions.q: How does Azure Hybrid Benefit apply to SQL Server on an Azure VM, compared to its vCore-model use in Lesson 9?
options: It lets you apply an existing SQL Server license (with Software Assurance) to the VM image so you pay Azure only for infrastructure, not for a license you already own
It only works on Azure SQL Database, never on VM-hosted SQL Server
It reduces the VM's storage cost, not its licensing cost
It requires giving up the ability to patch SQL Server yourself
questions.explain: On a VM this applies to the full retail SQL Server license cost, which the lesson calls often the single biggest cost lever in a real migration.

questions.q: What is the key difference between VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute for hybrid SQL connectivity?
options: VPN Gateway is an encrypted tunnel over the public internet; ExpressRoute is a private, dedicated circuit with no public internet involved at all
They are functionally identical with no meaningful difference
ExpressRoute only works for Azure SQL Database, never for VM-hosted SQL Server
VPN Gateway requires no encryption at all
questions.explain: Both are real options for connecting on-prem and Azure SQL workloads, differing in whether traffic touches the public internet.

questions.q: What does 'hybrid SQL' describe, per this lesson?
options: Architectures where some SQL Server workloads stay on-prem permanently by design while others run in Azure, connected over private networking
A temporary state during a migration that always ends with everything moved to Azure
Running SQL Server and Oracle side by side in the same environment
A purchasing model exclusive to Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: A common example given is on-prem Active Directory domain controllers with a SQL Server VM joining the same domain over ExpressRoute or VPN.

questions.q: What does Chapter 3 do differently from Chapter 2, per this lesson's closing note?
options: It revisits the same three-way deployment decision against real business requirements, with storage, scaling, and compliance factors added, rather than covering how to deploy each option
It re-teaches the same deployment steps for all three options from scratch
It removes SQL Server on an Azure VM from consideration entirely
It focuses exclusively on backup and restore procedures
questions.explain: Chapter 2 was one deployment option per lesson in depth; Chapter 3 picks the same decision back up as "which one fits this requirement," plus partitioning, compression, sharding, Azure Arc, and Fabric.
